3. How to schedule an MRI scan
3.1 Referral
An MRI scan can only be booked with a valid referral (medical order) from a hospital doctor. Self-referrals are not accepted.
3.2 Booking steps
1. Make sure your doctor has placed an MRI order in your medical record.
2. Book through the Radiology front desk (Ground Floor, Block B), the patient portal, or by calling the Radiology helpline.
3. Choose an available imaging slot. Slots are 30 minutes, Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 13:00.
4. Complete the MRI safety screening questionnaire at least 24 hours before the scan.
5. If you have insurance, the Insurance Desk will check coverage before your scan date.
3.3 Rescheduling and cancellation
Appointments can be rescheduled or cancelled up to 24 hours before the scan without charge.

3. How to schedule an MRI scan
3.1 Referral
An MRI scan can only be booked with a valid referral (medical order) from a hospital doctor. Self-referrals are not accepted.
3.2 Booking steps
1. Make sure your doctor has placed an MRI order in your medical record.
2. Book through the Radiology front desk (Ground Floor, Block B), the patient portal, or by calling the Radiology helpline.
3. Choose an available imaging slot. Slots are 30 minutes, Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 13:00.
4. Complete the MRI safety screening questionnaire at least 24 hours before the scan.
5. If you have insurance, the Insurance Desk will check coverage before your scan date.
3.3 Rescheduling and cancellation
Appointments can be rescheduled or cancelled up to 24 hours before the scan without charge.

4. Safety screening
Patients must tell the Radiology team if they have a pacemaker, cochlear implant, metal fragments, an insulin pump, or are pregnant. Some implants make MRI unsafe; the radiologist decides whether the scan can proceed.

5. Preparation on the day
5.1 Fasting for contrast scans
For MRI scans with contrast, patients must not eat for 4 hours before the scan. Water is allowed.
5.2 Arrival
Arrive 30 minutes before your slot. Remove all metal objects, jewellery and cards with magnetic strips.
5.3 Diabetic patients
Patients taking metformin who are scheduled for a contrast scan must inform the Radiology team; the referring physician will advise on medication.

6. Results
Reports are usually available within 48 hours and are shared with the referring doctor and on the patient portal.

3. Imaging with contrast
3.1 Fasting
Patients scheduled for imaging with contrast (CT or MRI) must not eat for 6 hours before the procedure. Small sips of water are allowed.
3.2 Kidney function
Check that a recent serum creatinine result is available for patients over 60 or with diabetes.

2. General preparation
2.1 Identity check
Confirm the patient's identity with two identifiers (full name and date of birth) before any procedure.
2.2 Allergies
Check and document allergies, especially to contrast agents, latex and antibiotics.

3. Imaging with contrast
3.1 Fasting
Patients scheduled for imaging with contrast (CT or MRI) must not eat for 6 hours before the procedure. Small sips of water are allowed.
3.2 Kidney function
Check that a recent serum creatinine result is available for patients over 60 or with diabetes.

4. Vital signs
Record blood pressure, pulse, temperature and oxygen saturation before the patient is transferred.

4. Required pre-operative tests
4.1 Tests for all patients
The following results must be available and recent before surgery:
• Complete Blood Count (CBC) – within 30 days of surgery
• Coagulation profile (PT/INR) – within 30 days of surgery
• 12-lead ECG – within 30 days of surgery
• Chest X-ray (PA view) – within 90 days of surgery
4.2 Additional tests for diabetic patients
Patients with diabetes need an HbA1c result within 90 days of surgery. The HbA1c must be below 8.0 % for elective surgery to proceed. If it is 8.0 % or above, the patient is referred to Endocrinology and surgery is postponed.
4.3 Pre-anaesthesia review
Every patient must complete a pre-anaesthesia review within 30 days before surgery.

5. Readiness checklist
Before the day of surgery the following must be confirmed:
1. Surgical consent form signed.
2. Fasting instructions given and acknowledged: no solid food for 8 hours and no clear fluids for 2 hours before surgery.
3. Diabetic patients: the plan for holding metformin and other diabetes medicines is confirmed with the physician.
4. An adult escort is arranged for discharge.

7. When surgery is postponed
If any required test is missing, expired or out of range, the surgical team will contact the patient to arrange the test and, if needed, a new surgery date.

6. Insurance pre-authorisation
For insured patients, insurance pre-authorisation must be approved before the scheduled date of elective surgery. If pre-authorisation is pending, the surgery date may be moved.

2.1 Documents required
• A government-issued photo identity document
• Contact phone number and address
• Insurance card (if the patient wants to use insurance)
• Previous medical records or referral letters (optional)
2.2 Steps
• Visit the Registration Counter (Ground Floor, Main Lobby), open 08:00 to 20:00 every day.
• Fill in the registration form or register online through the patient portal.
• Staff verify identity and create a unique Patient ID (format P followed by four digits).
• The patient receives a registration card and portal login details.

2. Planned admission
2.1 Before admission
• The treating doctor issues an admission advice note.
• The patient registers (see the Patient Registration SOP) and completes pre-admission tests if required.
• Insured patients submit the insurance card at the Insurance Desk at least 3 working days before admission for cashless approval.
2.2 On the day of admission
Report to the Admissions Desk (Ground Floor, Block A) at the time given in your admission letter. Bring your Patient ID, photo identity document, current medicines and previous reports.
2.3 Deposit
Patients without approved cashless insurance pay an admission deposit based on the estimated cost of the procedure and room type.

5. Attendants
One attendant may stay with an admitted patient in general wards and private rooms. Attendants receive an attendant pass at admission.

3. Emergency admission
Emergency patients are admitted directly through the Emergency Department. Registration and insurance formalities can be completed by a relative after the patient is stabilised.

2. Discharge criteria
A patient may be discharged when:
• Pain is controlled with tablets.
• The patient can walk with a walker or crutches and climb a few stairs with help.
• The wound is clean and dry.
• The physiotherapist has approved discharge.
Most patients go home 3 to 5 days after knee replacement surgery.

3. Wound care at home
Keep the dressing clean and dry. Do not soak the wound in a bath until the surgeon allows it. Stitches or clips are removed at the follow-up visit, usually 12 to 14 days after surgery.

5. Warning signs – contact the hospital immediately
• Fever above 38 °C
• Increasing redness, swelling or discharge from the wound
• Pain or swelling in the calf, or shortness of breath
• Sudden increase in pain

7. Before you leave
Collect your discharge summary, prescribed medicines and the final bill. Billing clearance must be completed at the Billing Counter before discharge.

1. Medical emergencies

In a medical emergency inside the hospital, alert the nearest staff member or press the red emergency call button. For emergencies outside the hospital, call the national emergency number.

4. Required pre-operative tests
4.1 Tests for all patients
The following results must be available and recent before surgery:
• Complete Blood Count (CBC) – within 30 days of surgery
• Coagulation profile (PT/INR) – within 30 days of surgery
• 12-lead ECG – within 30 days of surgery
• Chest X-ray (PA view) – within 90 days of surgery
4.2 Additional tests for diabetic patients
Patients with diabetes need an HbA1c result within 90 days of surgery. The HbA1c must be below 8.0 % for elective surgery to proceed. If it is 8.0 % or above, the patient is referred to Endocrinology and surgery is postponed.
4.3 Pre-anaesthesia review
Every patient must complete a pre-anaesthesia review within 30 days before surgery.
